headline: A potent winter storm keeps piling heavy snow on the Sierra, including the Mammoth area, through Friday morning, with a brief break before a weaker storm arrives Saturday afternoon or night and more storms possible Thanksgiving week.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: Moderate to heavy snow showers continue in the Sierra Thursday, with another 1–2 feet possible along the eastern Sierra crest (a 70% chance of at least 12 inches there) and 6–12 more inches possible at Mammoth, Truckee and South Lake Tahoe through early Friday morning. Lake level at Tahoe picks up 2–6 inches, while western Nevada and northeast California valleys get up to 2 inches and areas above 5,000 feet 2–6 inches. Snow levels stay below 6,000 feet, west winds gust to 50–60 mph on Sierra ridges tonight into Friday morning, and gusty winds hit western Nevada valleys and northeast California. Winter Storm Warnings run until 4 AM Friday for parts of the Sierra and Winter Weather Advisories until 7 PM this evening elsewhere; snow showers turn more scattered by late evening, though lake-effect snow is possible on the south and southeast sides of Pyramid Lake and Lake Tahoe tonight into early Friday.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Snow showers linger through late Friday morning, mainly around Tahoe, with up to 2–3 more inches in the Sierra and up to an inch in western Nevada; slush may turn to ice for the Friday morning commute, with lows in the teens in the Sierra and low to mid 20s in western Nevada. Friday stays very cold, about 15 degrees below average, and by Saturday morning lows drop to the single digits in the Sierra and low teens in western Nevada. A weaker storm moves in Saturday afternoon or night and lasts into early Monday, bringing 3–6 inches along the Sierra crest, up to 3 inches above 6,000 feet, and a trace to an inch even on valley floors including the Reno area, as the cold air keeps snow down to the valleys.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: Cold, winter-like temperatures continue into early next week. The pattern stays unsettled through Thanksgiving week, with more storms that could affect holiday travel, but forecasters have low confidence in the details so far.

watch_for: Hazardous Sierra travel through Friday morning from heavy snow and 50–60 mph ridge winds, plus icy roads on the Friday morning commute.
Snow totals from the Saturday night–Monday storm, including possible light snow on valley floors.
Timing and strength of storms during Thanksgiving travel week.
confidence: Forecasters are confident in heavy Sierra snow through Friday morning and a weaker storm late in the weekend, but have low confidence in the details for Thanksgiving week.
